title: sprint-orchestration-playbook-scenario-suite-v0-1
body:
Purpose
- Create a compact but operational playbook that binds the next 12-week sprint to company-level priorities and a public convocation (company event). This is meant to be an execution-first draft: terse, event-focused, and actionable.

Context / why now
- Usage has spiked in hosted API over the last 6 weeks; tail latency incidents in region-us-west have created internal priority shifts.
- We need an aligned plan for how Dedicated capacity, Private onboarding, and Console rollouts will be sequenced with clear owner-level accountability.
- This doc collects OKR drafts, a proposed convocation agenda for senior staff + company, and the decision timeline for SLAs and capacity commitments.

Topline proposed OKRs (draft)
Objective A — Stabilize platform SLOs and reduce production variance (owner: SRE lead)
  KR A1: Reduce 99th-percentile inference latency on hosted API (text gen) from 320ms to <=250ms for 95% of traffic by week 12.
  KR A2: Mean time to recovery (MTTR) for region incidents <= 22 minutes (rolling average) by end of sprint.
  KR A3: Prefix cache hit-rate >= 18% across top 50 customer prefixes.

Objective B — Deliver next-gen cost controls and dedicated capacity commitments (owner: Product + Ops)
  KR B1: Ship Reserved Instance pricing page + quota UI and have 3 pilot customers onboarded to Dedicated pools by week 8.
  KR B2: Reduce per-token inference cost (P95) by 12% via batching + quantization profiles in Optimize.
  KR B3: Launch internal cost-dashboard with per-route attribution and anomaly alerts (alert fidelity >= 80%).

Objective C — Developer velocity and rollout quality (owner: DevEx + Platform Eng)
  KR C1: Publish 6 SDK feature parity items + migration guide; adoption by 30% of active API keys.
  KR C2: Run 2 cross-team canary rollouts (Hosted -> Dedicated fallback) with automated rollback tests.
  KR C3: Ship prompt-eval harness and baseline alerting to detect quality regressions on 4 sample prompts.

Proposed convocation (company event) — 90 minute flow (draft)
- Opening (10m): CEO framing on why stabilization + cost focus matters now (tell the story, one metric to remember).
- Quick wins & customer spotlight (10m): demo of a Dedicated pilot (customer voice recorded).
- SRE heatmap (10m): 6-week incident trends, actionables, and escalation changes.
- Product priorities (15m): Reserve/Dedicated timeline + how this affects customer SLAs.
- Breakouts (20m): Small, mixed-function tables to surface blockers (ops, infra, product, sales). Each table captures 3 blockers + owner.
- AMA (15m): Pre-collected questions from staff + live q&a with execs.
- Close (10m): Clear asks + immediate next steps (what to do Monday morning).

Exec update bullets (one-pagers for ELT)
- Metric snapshot: hosted API requests +12% w/w; Dedicated signups +2 pilot conversions; NPS pilot feedback: 4.2/5 (supported).
- Risk callouts: kernel fallback mismatch on one quantized model (incurs 2x latency). Ops mitigation: temporary routing policy to avoid that model until kernel patch (ETA 10 days).
- Financial note: projected Dedicated revenue runway assumes 2 mid-market deals signed by week 10. If not, propose runway contingency (soft cap on burst autoscaling).
- Ask to execs: decision on increasing Dedicated capacity commit (yes/no) by Oct 22.

Risks and mitigations (short list)
- Risk: Shipping batching + quantization quickly could introduce subtle quality regressions for long-form generation.
  Mitigation: run offline eval harness, enforce holdback on top-10 customers until manual signoff.
- Risk: Convocation breakouts produce lots of action items but no owner follow-through.
  Mitigation: require table leads to create linear tickets during session and commit a 7-day followup check-in.
- Risk: SLA commitments misaligned with actual tail-latency performance.
  Mitigation: adopt conservative SLOs for public commitments + 1-month internal buffer.

Decisions needed (timeline)
- Oct 14: Confirm convocation agenda and presenters (owner: Leah Chen).
- Oct 18: ELT decision on Dedicated capacity commit (owner: Oliver Park).
- Oct 21: Approve public-facing OKR summary and marketing sync (owner: Product Marketing).
- Oct 25: Finalize canary roll procedures and rollback criteria (owner: Release Eng).

Breakouts — expected outputs (template)
- 3 blockers (short sentence each)
- Proposed owner + deadline (YYYY-MM-DD)
- A quick escalation path (who to loop in if blocked after 72 hours)

Quick notes to leads (style + constraints)
- Keep slides to 2 max per speaker, focused on one metric + one ask. Avoid operational deep-dives in the plenum.
- For the SRE heatmap: show trends, two remediation experiments, and what we need (people/permissions).
- For Product: show triage of top 5 feature requests that must be deprioritized if Capacity commit is denied.

Action items (initial)
- Leah: finalize convocation communication + send pre-read by Oct 10.
- Ravi (SRE): generate 6-week incident heatmap + annotated runbook excerpts by Oct 12.
- Samira (Product): solidify Dedicated pilot slide + customer quote by Oct 11.
- Marco (DevEx): readiness checklist for SDK migration guide + sample PRs by Oct 18.
- Jules (Release Eng): write rollback playbook + test checklist by Oct 25.

Unresolved questions (notes)
- Are we comfortable with a public SLO target that is within 10% of internal SLO? pros/cons?
- Do we want to publish an early-commit Dedicated reference architecture for pilot customers? (risk: leaks + support overhead)

References & links (for pre-read)
- Confluence: CI-ops-bridge-827 (operational playbook)
- JIRA: REINF-412 (Dedicated pricing + quota workstream)
- GitHub: ops-playbooks PR #89 (canary rollback template)
- Slack: #eng-cadence thread (discussion on convocation timing)

Appendix — convocation logistics (brief)
- Venue: virtual + regional watch parties (SF office + London office).
- Recording: will publish within 48 hours; execs should keep public statements to approved bullets.
- Feedback loop: anonymous pulse survey 24 hours post-event, 3 targeted prompts (clarity of asks, perceived progress, blockers surfaced).

Notes to self (very rough)
- Keep the tone optimistic but honest: show progress and concrete asks (money/people/time).
- Cross-check with legal on messaging about SLAs (esp. for Private deployments).

— end of draft —

Comments: This is intentionally more tactical than some of the high-level playbooks. The goal: create a tight bridge between ELT decisions and team-level sprint commitments. Use this draft as the single source to produce the event slides, ELT one-pager, and the follow-up Linear ticket set.
